title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
Flora is experiencing an uptick in the theft of items left in vehicles and Flora Police are urging people to take steps to protect their valuables and their vehicles.  That was one of the takeaways from Monday’s Flora City Council Meeting.

But before the regular meeting got underway, there was public hearing about Flora’s application for a $1.5 Million Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Community Development Block Grant.  If approved, Flora will use the grant to install over 12,000 feet of sewer line, manhole rehabilitation, point repairs, trench backfill, traffic control and related costs.  Half of the proposed funding will benefit individuals with low-to-moderate incomes.  The hearing was an opportunity for public comments about the proposed project.  With no comments made, the hearing adjourned.  City Administrator Mike Stanford did note that if the grant application is approved, these improvements would help with the plans for Flora’s new wastewater treatment plant.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the regular meeting to order at 4:30 Monday afternoon with the first item of business opening the floor to public comments.  Arriel Dulaney with the Flora Chamber of Commerce was the first to address the group.  She asked the City of Flora to approve the altered traffic flow for the Flora Halloween Parade on Saturday, October 31st.  She was urged to consult with Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger, and they briefly touched base with a future meeting to be worked out.  A motion was made to approve her request, and commissioners quickly approved it without dissent.

Next, Nikki Green with Flora Tourism also had a request to close part of 2nd Street on July 11th for their Community Market Christmas in July event.  Green explained they want to use part of 2nd Street and possibly the Flora Library parking lot for a food truck.  Her request was also approved unanimously.

As the comments ended, Mayor Spicer asked for the meeting agenda and consent agenda to be approved.  The latter included past meeting minutes and the warrant list for the last half of June.  Both were approved without dissent.

Under regular business, the mayor thanked all of the volunteers who helped put on Flora’s July 4th event on Saturday and said the fireworks were wonderful.  She recognized that watching them was a small part of the overall effort and the city made America 250 one to remember in Flora and was well worth it and she thanked everyone involved for their contribution.  Spicer sought to appoint Cassie Devore to the Flora Tourism Committee to a two-year term that expires July 6, 2028.  The measure was approved unanimously.

Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger began his brief comments with a thank you to Flora Police Reserve Officers for their help over the holiday weekend with the overall event and especially for help with traffic control Saturday night.  This is also when Chief Ruger made mention that they are seeing the burglary of valuables taken from vehicles in the local area.  He encourages people not to leave valuable in their vehicles and to keep them locked when they are not around.  Be especially aware when parking in areas where lighting is not always available.  Don’t leave windows rolled down.  Take your keys with you every time.  Never leave valuables like wallets, cellphone, laptops, or other electronic items in plain sight.  If you see someone acting suspiciously, call law enforcement.  Ruger closed by noting they have some persons of interest in mind, but the best advice is to take action to protect yourself.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford had five action items to present.  First was an ordinance approving the awarding of a bid and the sale of real estate for 315 Austin Ave.  the bid of $1,250 submitted by Bea Jay Laufhton was approved unanimously.  Commissioners also approved an ordinance approving the awarded of bid and sale of real estate for 847 W. Maple at a price of $1,200 that was submitted by Act Tire and Auto, LLC.  Next, members approved an ordinance approving the awarding of bid and sale of real estate for 144 Shady submitted by Tara Stanford in the amount of $100.  Stanford paused for a moment to announce that the City of Flora applied for another Strong Communities Grant in the amount of $270,000 on June 30.  The Strong Communities Program helps local governments buy, fix up, or demolish abandoned houses and then sell them.  The Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) administers the program to fight neighborhood decay by turning empty eyesores into safe, affordable homes or productive green spaces.  Commissioners next approved a funding resolution with the Illinois Department of Transportation in the amount of $34,630.  He said that sometime back a crosswalk project on U.S. Routes 45/50 and was supposed to cost $10,900, but it ended up with the higher price tag mentioned.  Stanford stressed that it is MFT eligible.  The final item of the meeting was Stanford’s request to approve a Community Partnership Agreement with CEFS for a three-year period that expires July 5, 2029, to help with the projects CEFS is involved in the local community.  The measure was approved without dissent.

title: EDWARDS SENTENCED FOR STABBING
full_story:
Trevor J. Edwards, 25 of Fairfield was sentenced in connection with the May, 2022 stabbing of Gregory Hughes in Clay County.  As part of a plea deal, Edwards entered a guilty plea to a reduced charge of battery, a Class-A misdemeanor and was placed on 12 months of non-reporting conditional discharge.  He had been initially charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, a Class-3 felony.

The charges against Edwards were filed in May of last year while he was serving time in a federal penitentiary for trafficking in counterfeit goods.  The case dates back to May 1, 2022 when Edwards stabbed a Hughes in the side during an altercation.  Advanced investigative technology was used to link Edwards to the weapon used in the stabbing, Clay County Sheriff’s officials said.

In addition to conditional discharge, Edwards was sentenced to 364 days in the county jail with credit for 182 days already served.  The judge ordered Edwards to have no contact with the victim in the case, Gregory Hughes, and ordered him to pay a $1,000 fine and $464 in court related fees.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Frequent rains and saturated fields have created challenges for wheat growers trying to harvest the crop in central and northern Illinois.  USDA reported Monday wheat harvest statewide reached 78%, falling behind both last year (84%) and average pace (87%).

There were 4.5 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending July 5th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 78.4 degrees, 2.9 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.45 inches, 0.31 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 2% very short, 6% short, 66% adequate, and 26% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 2% very short, 10% short, 69% adequate, and 19% surplus.

Corn silking reached 17%, just behind the 5 year average of 19%.  Corn Dough reached 1% equal to the 5 year average.  Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 9% poor, 29% fair, 45% good, 13% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 33%, compared to the 5-year average of 29%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 8% compared to the 5 year average of 3%.  Soybeans condition was rated 4% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 45% good, and 13% excellent.

Winter wheat harvested for grain reached 78%, compared to the 5-year average of 87%.  Winter Wheat condition was rated 1% very poor, 5% poor, 19% fair, 59% good, and 16% excellent.

title: DEATH INVESTIGATION
full_story:
Marion County Sheriff Kevin Cripps says an investigation is underway into the death of 56-year-old Bryan Hester of Salem while he was an inmate at the Marion County Jail.  Cripps says Hester was found unresponsive in his cell in what is believed to be a suicide attempt.

The sheriff reports that correctional staff and emergency personnel immediately initiated life-saving measures.  However, despite all efforts, Hester was pronounced deceased at 6:36 Sunday evening by Marion County Coroner Claude Howell.

In accordance with standard protocol, the Illinois State Police have been requested to conduct an independent investigation.

Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

title: 2 YEARS OF ACTIVELY ENGAGED
full_story:
The Illinois Farm Bureau is celebrating two academic years of the Illinois Farm Bureau Actively Engaged Student of the Month.  The program was launched in the fall of 2024.  A total of 20 students have been honored and they were recognized at a special banquet last month at the Aaron Leetch Club at Illinois State University’s Hancock Stadium.

The recognition program is based on FFA, 4H/County fair, IHSA and student club/organization participation.  Max Main was involved in all of that while at ROWVA.  He now attends Purdue University.

Both Haven Cash and Ava Fleener from the North Clay FFA have been named Actively Engaged Students of the Month.

To see all of the Illinois Farm Bureau Actively Engaged Students of the Month, visit farmweeknow.com/activelyengaged. Nominations for the 2026/2027 academic year open in August.

title: YOUTH CROP SCOUTING COMPETITION
full_story:
The Illinois Youth Crop Scouting Competition will break new ground August 4th for high school students interested in agronomy.

The fifth annual event remains an opportunity for students to work as a team, explore, share their knowledge and help solve current crop-related issues.  Most competitors are 4-H or FFA members, but all high schoolers in grades 9-12 are welcome.

This year, for the first time, students will judge corn, soybeans and a mystery alternative crop in a field plot provided by the University of Illinois Crop Sciences Department.

Meagan Diss, competition coordinator and commercial agriculture specialist with U of I Extension, told FarmWeek “We previously used greenhouse grow outs.  This is the first time it’s in plots.”  “It’s a chance for students to get into the field and showcase their skills in a real environment,” she said.

Getting this real field experience will help the two top Illinois teams when they compete at a higher level against students from other states in the Regional Youth Crop Scouting Competition.

Further, for the first time, the regional competition will be held in Illinois.  Two teams from each of the six states; Illinois, Iowa, Indiana, Minnesota, Nebraska and Kentucky; will compete September 12th at the same location at U of I’s Crop Sciences Research and Education Center in Champaign.  Competitors must have already placed first or second in their home states to qualify.

“It’s the best of the best,” Diss said of the regional competition.

Registration is filling up for the 10 spots available for the Illinois Youth Crop Scouting Competition.  It’s nearly full, with only room for a couple more teams, Diss said, adding teams must apply by July 1st so there is time to get study materials to them.

All teams must include two to five students and an adult coach.

During the daylong contest, the teams rotate through various crop testing stations set up in corn and soybean fields to test their knowledge of topics such as weeds, insects, disease identification, corn and soybean growth stages, abiotic disorders, pesticide application and integrated pest management.

“While rotating through stations, students get to handle the crops themselves, ask questions and have conversations with university researchers and experts from the field,” Diss said.

University staff judge the teams and select the winners, the top four teams win cash prizes of $500, $300, $200 and $100, sponsored by industry and university partners.

Register by July 1st at go.illinois.edu/CropScouting.  For more information, contact Diss at [email protected] or 217-300-5386.

title: EFFINGHAM SHOOTING
full_story:
The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office requested the Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 8 to investigate a shooting incident at St. John’s Lutheran Church on Jefferson Avenue in Effingham.

On Sunday, at approximately 9:27 am, St. John’s Lutheran Church security contacted Effingham Police Department to report a suspicious vehicle and suspicious man inside the church wishing to speak with the pastor, no church service were occurring at the time.  The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office responded to the church and located the man a short time later.  The suspicious vehicle was reported stolen out of Marion County.  Officers from both agencies attempted to restrain the man.  During the struggle, the man produced a firearm, which discharged, and the man was struck.  The man was taken to a local hospital and later transported by helicopter to a regional hospital with life-threatening injuries.  No one else was injured in this incident.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Department says the vehicle had been stolen in Kinmundy at 8:55 Sunday morning.

This was an isolated incident and there is no known threat to the community at this time.

This is an active investigation, and no additional information is available at this time.
